title: Build it or buy it
description: How a team decides whether to buy a tool, build one, or stop and come back later.

states.name: Frame the need
states.description: Someone has said the team needs a thing. Before comparing anything, you are writing down the problem in terms of what people cannot do today.

states.name: Separate must from nice
states.description: You are splitting the wish list into requirements that would rule an option out and preferences that would not. Only the first kind decides anything.
states.annotation: If every requirement is a must, the list has not been thought about yet.

states.name: Survey the market
states.description: You are looking at what already exists, including the boring option nobody is excited about, and checking each against the must-have list.

states.name: Run a trial
states.description: One candidate looks close enough to test with real data and real users, on the workflow you actually care about rather than the demo.

states.name: Check the constraints
states.description: The tool works. Now legal, security and procurement look at data residency, access control and the contract before anyone commits.
states.annotation: Start this earlier than feels necessary. It is the step that most often adds weeks.

states.name: Nothing on the market fits
states.description: Every candidate fails a must-have, or the ones that pass are priced for a much larger company. Building is now a serious option.

states.name: Estimate the build
states.description: You are costing the build honestly: not just the first version, but the on-call, the migrations and the person who owns it in two years.

states.name: Buy it
states.description: A vendor meets the must-haves and clears the constraints. You are signing, planning the rollout, and writing down what would make you reconsider.

states.name: Build it
states.description: The need is specific enough and the team has the capacity to own it. You are naming the owner before writing any code.

states.name: Defer the decision
states.description: Neither option is justified right now. You are recording what you learned and the condition that would restart this, so the next person does not repeat the survey.
states.annotation: A deferred decision with written reasons is a real outcome. An undocumented one gets rediscovered every six months.

transitions.label: Write down what must be true
The team cannot agree on the problem
At least one candidate looks close
A constraint rules the vendor out
Revisit which requirements are really must-haves
transitions.description: Often one must-have is doing all the ruling out.

transitions.label: The true cost is too high for now
Look again with a bigger budget
